2609.31506.title: Evaluating Cultural Awareness of LLMs for Haitian Creole
2609.31506.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit substantial performance disparities between high- and low-resource languages. Beyond lower task performance, they often fail to capture the cultural norms and values of underrepresented communities. In this work, we present the first systematic evaluation of cultural awareness in LLMs for Haitian Creole, a language spoken by millions but severely underrepresented in digital resources. We assess cultural awareness along four complementary dimensions---specificity, bias, diversity, and variation---using a benchmark of culturally salient prompts curated by native speakers in a text infilling setting. Our results reveal a clear gap between cultural awareness in Haitian Creole and higher-resource French, with Haitian performance being more uneven across domains and more affected by French linguistic interference. Story generation further reveals recurring portrayals of Haitian characters through hardship and resilience, showing that even positive characterizations can encode stereotypical narratives. Our code, benchmark, and evaluation framework are publicly available.
2609.31506.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在高資源語言和低資源語言之間表現出顯著的性能差異。<lb/>除了任務性能較低之外，它們通常無法捕捉到代表性不足社群的文化規範和價值觀。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們首次系統性地評估了LLMs在海地克里奧語中的文化意識，這是一種由數百萬人使用但在數位資源中嚴重不足的語言。<lb/>我們沿著四個互補的維度評估文化意識——具體性、偏見、多樣性和變異——使用由母語者在文本填充環境中策劃的文化顯著提示基準。<lb/>我們的結果顯示海地克里奧語的文化意識與資源較高的法語之間存在明顯的差距，海地的表現跨領域更不均衡，且更受法語語言干擾的影響。<lb/>故事生成進一步揭示了海地角色在艱難與韌性中的重複描繪，顯示即使是正面的角色刻畫也可能編碼刻板印象敘事。<lb/>我們的代碼、基準和評估框架均已公開。
2609.31506.author: Christelle Clervilsson et.al.
